reason: The kidney filter and approaching blood are the obvious starting point for following filtration.
expectation: The nephron will filter fluid from the blood into its tubule.

effect: The filter lets fluid and small substances into the tubule while retaining blood cells and most proteins. Next I can follow recovery.
reaction: It was useful to see that useful small substances enter the filtrate too.
reason: The tubule transporters appear to be the next piece for selectively recovering substances from the filtered sample.
expectation: The transporters will return some useful dissolved substances toward the blood.

effect: The tubule recovers glucose and other useful substances; I can now follow water recovery.
reaction: It clarified why filtering glucose out of blood does not mean losing it all in urine.
reason: The water-permeable tubule picture shows water moving back toward blood, matching the next recovery step.
expectation: Some water will move from the tubule fluid back toward the blood.

effect: Water has returned to the blood while wastes remain in the tubule, so I can follow the remaining fluid into urinary drainage.
reaction: The sequence makes it clearer that filtration is followed by recovery.
reason: Urinary drainage is shown leading from the kidney toward the ureter and bladder, making it the apparent next route for the remaining sample.
expectation: The remaining fluid will enter the urinary drainage route as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid is urine, and it travels through a ureter to the bladder. The filtering goal is complete; the urinary organs still need connecting.
reaction: The path from filtering to the bladder is clear now.
reason: The kidney pair has a named ureter slot, and the ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will fit onto the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are attached to the kidney pair; the bladder slot remains.
reaction: The named slot made that step straightforward.
reason: The bladder fits the remaining named slot and receives urine from the ureters.
expectation: The bladder will attach to the urinary organ assembly.

effect: The bladder is attached, completing the kidney-to-bladder route; the urinary organs still need connecting to the body.
reaction: The route is straightforward after following the urine sample.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the urinary organs to the body, so the completed kidney assembly belongs with the body model.
expectation: The urinary organs will connect to the body and its circulation.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to the body's circulation, with urine draining through the ureters to the bladder. Both goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the organ route connected to the body after following the filtered sample.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering useful substances after filtering was most worthwhile: it showed why glucose entering the tubule does not normally mean losing it in urine.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was straightforward but a little repetitive because the named slots already gave away the pairings.

surprise.text: I was surprised that glucose is filtered out and then almost all recovered in healthy kidneys.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and named slots made the sequence understandable.

continue.text: I would probably continue: following the sample from filtration through recovery made the kidney's job clearer, and I would be curious to see another system explained that way.
